page.layout: One column of verse, running from the top to the middle of the page; below it, right-aligned, the initials "A. T. H."; below that, centred, "FINIS."

main_text.p:
Omnia complectens, nulli tamen ipse prebensus:
Omnibus infusus, labis at omnis inops:

Abripe me sursum, miro cum flamine mirus
Allabens lutea pectora fece laua:

Inq; tuam rape naturam, correptaq; flammis
Attenua, & formans attenuata foue.

Unum sim tecum, maneam tibi semper adhaerens,
Numen idem veluti cum genitore manes.

Plasma tuum instaura nativo crimine fissum,
Assere & amissum vindice iure tibi:

Ut mea damna meo fatear tribuamq; furori,
Atq; accepta tibi commoda cuncta feram:

Qui mira bonitate malum convertere nostrum
In tua lætaris, Christe benigne, bona.

Pectoris ah hyemem, si non pietate calescat
Tam mira, & vero flagret amore tui.

Attonitum ah mentis somnum tristemq; veternum,
Ni vigilet tantis illa agitata bonis.

Hoc opus haud nostrae: me Patris o alma voluptas
Christe mihi occidas, sic tibi vivus agam:

Meq; mihi excidas, vti quo palmes adorner
Florescamq; tibi, marcidus ipse mihi.

Incipiam nihil esse mihi: sic omnia abunde
Adveniant gremio suppeditata tuo.

page.notes:
Uncertain readings: "Allabens" (line 4) may be a blackletter-style initial, copied as read; "fouè" in line 6 read as "foue"; "Hoc opus haud nostrae: me" has a mark over the o of "ô" that is not clear. The printed "prebenfus" and similar long-s forms are rendered with plain s. Verse grouped into couplets by the visible spacing; line breaks within each couplet are shown with
.
